independent.summary: Baseline mode cannot express "could not collect": if production is entirely unreachable (DNS/Railway down), every probe returns status 0 / ok:false, the file is written with five red checks and the process exits 0, so the run proceeds. That baseline then makes any genuine post-merge breakage classify as 'pre-existing' (ok:true) and a broken merge stands — the one case the item says must still block is only detected when the file itself cannot be written or parsed, not when the probes never reached production.

Compare mode exits 1 for both a real regression and a blocked/uncollectable baseline (`verdict.blocked || !verdict.ok`), so a runner with autoRevert:true keyed on the exit code will git-revert a healthy merge when the baseline file is missing or corrupt — the item requires that case to block, never to revert. Distinguishing them requires parsing the JSON, which the RUNBOOK does not instruct.

Checks are not individually guarded: an uncaught local error (e.g. fs.writeFileSync of the widget body to a full or read-only tmpdir, or fs.rmSync failing) rejects runSmoke, crashes the process with a nonzero exit in compare mode, and is indistinguishable from a regression — reverting healthy code for a fault on the runner, the exact class of mistake the item exists to stop.

classify() iterates only `after.checks`, so a check that was green at baseline but absent from the post-deploy result (renamed id, a check dropped from runSmoke) is silently omitted from the comparison and can never be reported as a regression; only the inverse direction (new check absent from baseline) is handled and tested.

isMain is computed by string-concatenating `file://` + path.resolve(argv[1]) instead of pathToFileURL, so a repo or worktree path containing a character that import.meta.url percent-encodes (space, '#', '?') makes the comparison false; the script then falls through, does nothing, and exits 0 — in compare mode that reads as "nothing regressed" and the gate silently passes.

The script has no deploy-landing retry, yet the health check hard-fails on a commit mismatch, so a single --compare invocation issued before Railway finishes deploying yields a `health` regression and triggers auto-revert of a good merge; the 30s/12min polling requirement exists only as RUNBOOK prose, which is precisely the re-implemented-from-prose failure mode this file was written to eliminate.

grades.reason: classify() explicitly returns blocked:true for a missing/non-array baseline (smoke.mjs:161-163) and the CLI wraps the read/parse in try/catch (smoke.mjs:200-204), with a dedicated test covering it.
The JSON.parse of the baseline is inside a try/catch at smoke.mjs:201 that leaves `baseline` null, which classify() turns into a blocked verdict — nothing throws.
checkHealth guards the commit assertion with `if (expectCommit && ...)` (smoke.mjs:63), so a missing --expect-commit skips the comparison entirely rather than always failing.
checkHealth validates that the body parses as JSON, that mongo === 1, and (when given) the commit (smoke.mjs:59-65); a non-JSON or field-less body is reported as a failure.

The test does cover that case (`classify(run(chk('chat', null)), run(chk('chat', false)))` asserts 'skipped'), and classifying an uncomparable check as a regression would contradict the item's design, so both halves of the claim are untrue.

triageGrades.reason: No authentication or authorization logic is added or changed — the script only forwards an existing admin key in a header to an already-protected endpoint.
LEO_ADMIN_API_KEY is read from env and sent to its own API; no secret is stored, logged, or committed (the baseline file is gitignored and contains no credentials).
Nothing in the diff touches billing, pricing, quota, or Stripe; the smoke entity is plan `infinity`, and an incidental Claude API call is not the money category.
The change rewrites the condition under which the auto-revert (git revert + push to main) fires and adds filesystem writes/removals, so destructive behaviour is genuinely in scope.
smoke.mjs newly fetches api.leo-ai.chat/health, leo-ai.app plus its bundle, POST /chat, /api/admin/search, and /demo/chatbot.js.
The diff rewrites the merge/deploy/smoke/revert gate in RUNBOOK.md and adds a new verification step, which is squarely the release pipeline.

summary: All five local findings are false positives that assert missing handling the diff plainly contains (baseline parse guard, health validation, expect-commit guard, skipped-check test), it missed every real gap — chiefly that an unreachable-production baseline is recorded as all-red instead of blocking and that compare mode cannot distinguish "blocked" from "regression" by exit code — and its triage got auth, money, and release wrong.
